songInfo.title: The Sky Is Crying
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: C - Eb - F - G - Bb - C
scalesUsed.application: Forms the core of Stevie Ray Vaughan's slow 12/8 blues lead vocabulary in the 8th and 13th fret Albert King boxes (sounding in B due to Eb tuning)

scalesUsed.notes: C - D - E - G - A - C
scalesUsed.application: Blended with minor pentatonic by curling the minor third (Eb) up a quarter-step toward the major third (E) over the C7 tonic chord

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Deep, weeping 12/8 slow Texas blues combining dominant 7th/9th harmony with ferocious Albert King-inspired minor-over-major string bending
keyAndScale.keySignature: 0 sharps/flats (in fretboard shapes; sounds a half-step lower in B7 due to Eb tuning)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: A minor is the relative minor of C major

mainProgression.progression: I7 - IV9 - I7 - V9 - IV9 - I7 - V7
mainProgression.progressionDescription: Classic 12-bar slow blues in 12/8 time with a quick-change IV9 in bar 2 and a chromatic walk-up into the V9 turnaround.
mainProgression.description: Classic 12-bar slow blues in 12/8 time with a quick-change IV9 in bar 2 and a chromatic walk-up into the V9 turnaround.

sectionProgressions.description: Opens with SRV's stinging 13th-fret Albert King Box bends over a slow 12/8 quick-change blues foundation
Moves to the 4-chord (F9) for two bars where lead lines target the flat-3rd (Eb) before resolving back to C7
Climactic V-IV-I descent finishing on a biting Hendrix/SRV dominant 7#9 turnaround chord
C minor pentatonic Box 1 (8th fret) and Albert King Box 2 (13th fret) slow blues phrasing

harmonicFunction: C7 (I7) - Dominant seventh tonic establishing the gritty slow-blues home center
F9 (IV9) - Lush dominant ninth subdominant chord adding Texas-blues sophistication in bars 2, 5, and 6
G9 / G7#9 (V9) - Dominant fifth chord driving the emotional peak of bar 9 and the bar 12 turnaround

techniques.name: Albert King Box Multi-Step String Bending & 12/8 Slow Blues Phrasing
techniques.description: Executing massive 1-to-2-step bends on the B and high E strings in the upper pentatonic extension ('Albert King Box') while riding the guitar volume knob for dramatic dynamic swells

notes: Albert King Box (Key of C): Frets 11-13 on B and high E strings
sequence: Position your hand at the 11th–13th frets on the G, B, and high E strings (Pentatonic Box 2 / Albert King Box)
Bend the 13th fret B string (C) up a full step to D, or 1.5 steps to Eb, using three fingers for support
Release down to the 11th fret B string (Bb) and resolve to the root C on the 13th fret B or 10th fret D string
Comp behind the vocals using light 9th-chord slides (E9 → F9) and raked triad double-stops
tips: Pre-rake the muted D and G strings right before striking a bent high note to get SRV's percussive, explosive attack
Use your index and middle fingers tightly behind your ring finger to push bends cleanly without fatiguing
Roll your Stratocaster volume knob down to 6 for the quiet vocal verses, then crank it to 10 for the solos

sections.name: Intro Albert King Box Lead Call
sections.technique: Albert King Box Multi-Step String Bending
sections.description: SRV's iconic opening slow-blues lead statement in the 11th–13th fret Albert King box over C7 and F9.
notes: Attack the 13th-fret B string and 11th-fret high E string with a fierce pick rake
Let every bent note weep with wide, controlled wrist vibrato

sections.name: Slow Blues 9th-Chord Rhythm Comping
sections.description: Warm, spacious 12/8 rhythm guitar comping using C7, F9, and G9 voicings.
notes: Slide into F9 from a half-step below (E9 at the 7th fret)
Keep the rhythm sparse and supportive behind the vocal line
Accent beats 4, 7, and 10 softly in the 12/8 meter

sections.name: 8th-Position C Minor Pentatonic Flurry
sections.description: Classic SRV Box 1 C minor pentatonic run at the 8th fret finishing with a slightly bent minor third.
notes: Keep your index finger anchored as a mini-barre at the 8th fret
Curl the 11th-fret B string (Eb) up slightly toward the major third (E)
Resolve decisively to the root C on the 10th fret of the D string

guitar.recommended: 1959/1962 Fender Stratocaster ('Number One') with heavy-gauge strings (.012 or .013 set tuned to Eb)
alternatives: Fender Stevie Ray Vaughan Signature Stratocaster
guitar.pickup: Neck single-coil pickup (or Neck + Middle position for glassy comping)

amp.recommended: 1964 Fender Vibroverb (with 15-inch speaker) & Fender Super Reverb

settings.gain: 5 (cranked clean tube amp on the verge of thick power-tube breakup)

effects.distortion: Ibanez TS9 or TS808 Tube Screamer (Drive low at 9 o'clock, Level high at 3 o'clock)
effects.other: Heavy celluloid pick played with the rounded shoulder for fat attack

beginner.title: 12/8 Slow Blues Count & 9th Chords
steps: Internalize the slow 12/8 blues count (four groups of three eighth notes per bar)
Learn the movable C7 (8th fret E), F9 (8th fret A), and G9 (10th fret A) chord shapes
Play through the 12-bar quick-change blues structure at 52 BPM

intermediate.title: 8th-Fret Minor Pentatonic & Half-Step Slides
steps: Add half-step approach slides into F9 (from E9) and G9 (from F#9)
Learn the 8th-position C minor pentatonic Box 1 licks and quarter-step blue-note curls
Alternate between two bars of rhythm comping and two bars of lead fills

advanced.title: Albert King Box Bends & SRV Dynamics
steps: Master the 11th–13th fret Albert King Box multi-step bends with rake attack
Control solo dynamics from whisper-quiet finger-picked phrases to roaring full-volume bends
Perform a complete two-chorus slow blues solo with authentic Texas phrasing

commonMistakes: Rushing the slow 52 BPM tempo instead of letting the 12/8 triplets breathe
Under-bending the 13th-fret B string in the Albert King Box so it sounds out of tune
Using only one finger to bend instead of reinforcing with the index and middle fingers
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Slow 12/8 ninth-chord comping (C7 - F9 - G9) with half-step slides
5 minutes: Intonation drill matching 13th-fret B-string bends to fretted target notes (15th and 16th frets)
5 minutes: Rake attack + vibrato control in the 8th-fret C minor pentatonic box
5 minutes: Full slow-blues improvisation over a 12-bar C7 backing track
focusAreas: Percussive left-hand muting during pick rakes
Expressive wrist vibrato on sustained bent notes
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 156 BPM (clicking every eighth note of the 12/8 bar) to lock in the triplet subdivisions
Once solid, set metronome to 52 BPM (clicking the four dotted-quarter beats) and feel the triplet swing internally
Practice starting phrases on beat 2 or beat 3 rather than always on beat 1
